To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liquid level in a freeze-drying vial has an important impact on the acoustic and bubble field, and thus on the ice nucleation process during the freezing step.
the acoustic field and the bubble location are strongly affected by the liquid level in insonified vials used for the freeze-drying process.

(i) the acoustic field saturate at high vibration amplitudes in insonified vials, (ii) a secondary bubble structure can be formed at high liquid levels, and (iii) the bubble field and the ice crystal distribution in the frozen sample may be affected by the liquid level in insonified free-drying vials, which is an important result for the pharmaceutical industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction and the understanding of the acoustic and cavitation fields in insonificated vials used for lyophilization.
the prediction and the understanding of acoustic fields in small cavities and with the influence of these fields on freeze-drying.
the development of a nonlinear model of the acoustics and bubble fields in freeze-drying vial and its application to the design of the freezing step of the freeze-drying process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the acoustic and bubble field in freeze-drying vial are strongly influenced by the liquid level and the vibration amplitude, and that a linear model is not sufficient to predict the acoustic field in such a small volume.
the acoustic field in freeze-drying vial is complex and cannot be captured by simple linear models.
, in freeze-drying, the acoustic field in a vial depends on the vibration amplitude, the liquid level, and the liquid's thermodynamic conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear acoustic and bubble fields can be computed in insonified vials, and that these fields are strongly influenced by the vibration amplitude and liquid level.
the acoustic and bubble structures in insonified vials are much more complex than previously thought, and should be carefully taken into account in order to optimize the freeze-drying process.
we have shown how to predict the acoustic field and the bubble field in freeze-drying vial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acoustic field in a freeze-drying vial is not necessarily a simple plane wave, and the bubble field can be quite complex.
, to predict the final product quality, it may not be enough to consider only the linear acoustic field in a vial, but rather the nonlinear acoustic field in the vial should be taken into account.
, to avoid ice crystals of too large a size, it is crucial to keep the liquid level in vials used in freeze-drying below 1 cm.
